units.translation: ⟦1⟧ = ⟦2⟧ is, as Or. ⟦3⟧ designates? One has (see Wecklein Einl. p. 19 note, after Blomfield on ⟦4⟧) derived ⟦5⟧ also directly from ⟦6⟧, as belongs to ⟦7⟧, so that it actually denotes the wandering spirit. Another difficulty is the inflection, because in Cramer's Anecd. Oxon. I, 62 it is noted: ⟦8⟧ (namely ⟦9⟧) ⟦10⟧. ⟦11⟧ "⟦12⟧" (Frg. 90 Ddf.), and Bk. Anecd. 382, 10 ⟦13⟧, ⟦14⟧. ⟦15⟧ "⟦16⟧". Nauck has brilliantly conjectured that in the original version ⟦17⟧ was quoted from the Ixion, 〈⟦18⟧〉 ⟦19⟧ but from this passage of the Eumenides, according to which one would have to write thus.
⟦1⟧ and -⟦2⟧ below 922 and often A., also Euripides Hek. 538 etc.; actually Ionic from ⟦3⟧.
⟦1⟧ only here and Frg. 147; ⟦2⟧ has Hesychios.

It seems necessary, in order to bring order into the sentences, with Prien and Paley to write ⟦1⟧ and ⟦2⟧; the accusatives are easily explained by assimilation, and other changes are not so easy. (⟦3⟧ | ⟦4⟧, with close binding of the verses, is, as Sidgwick notes, less surprising in Sophocles than in A.; see however on V. 800.) The thought is illustrated by V. 276 ff. and again 445 ff.: the expiation of the fresh blood has long been accomplished, before which act the polluted person was allowed to approach no one and speak to no one, so as not to infect them; now there is no longer any danger, especially since he has since been together with so many, without harm to them (284f.). This therefore must ⟦5⟧ mean (⟦6⟧ ⟦7⟧, do not lose their force);

⟦1⟧ rubbed on, rubbed off against, so that the edge is, as it were, blunted. Explaining (as so often in this play one passage explains another by repetition) 451f. ⟦2⟧, therefore ⟦3⟧ = ⟦4⟧ here, and this = way (by land as by water). P. Menge (de poetarum scaenicorum gr. dictione p. 66) indeed wants to understand "vehicle" = ship, comparing ⟦5⟧; but the land routes then fall out, on which Or. had also met with many, and there follows the epexegesis ⟦6⟧ (adverb., as often Hdt. Thukyd.) ⟦7⟧. As in the epexegesis the present ⟦8⟧ is also correct;
long ago we consecrated these things to other houses and passable and flowing paths
